circleci-migrate is v2-first. The vast majority of operations use the CircleCI API v2 (/api/v2/). The remaining surfaces are:
the legacy v1.1 API for settings not exposed by v2 (feature flags, project follow, additional SSH keys, project API tokens); the runner API v3 on runner.circleci.com for self-hosted runner resource classes; the private /api/private/ endpoint on circleci.com for App-org project discovery and a few org settings (contacts); the private CIAM endpoints on app.circleci.com for groups, SSO state, and org/project role grants; the graphql-unstable endpoint for orb-source introspection. The private endpoints are unofficial and may change — see the private-endpoint risk note. Each surface is documented explicitly below.
All requests carry a Circle-Token header and a User-Agent header in the form circleci-migrate/. The main host is configurable via --host (env CIRCLECI_CLI_HOST, CIRCLECI_HOST, or CIRCLE_URL; default: https://circleci.com). The private CIAM endpoints always target app.circleci.com and the runner API always targets runner.circleci.com (or the equivalent for Server installs); all use the same token.
Secret values are never returned by any API version. The CircleCI API masks every environment-variable value everywhere it appears. Capturing real values requires running inside a CircleCI job (see Moving secret values).
data.circleci-graphql-api-orb-inline#CircleCI:
The orb inline command fetches private orb source via the CircleCI GraphQL API. Unlike the REST endpoints above, this uses the graphql-unstable endpoint:
POST https://circleci.com/graphql-unstable The request carries a Circle-Token header and a JSON body with a query field. The query used to fetch orb source is:
query OrbSource($orbVersionRef: String!) { orbVersion(orbVersionRef: $orbVersionRef) { source } } orbVersionRef is the fully qualified orb reference from the config's orbs: stanza (e.g. awesomecicd/circleci-org-migration@0.8.0). Public orbs are fetched without a token; private orbs require a token that belongs to a user or machine-user with access to that orb's namespace. A null source in the response is treated as "orb not found or not accessible."
Why graphql-unstable? Orb source is not exposed by the REST API v2. The graphql-unstable endpoint is the canonical way to introspect orb content and is used by the CircleCI CLI for the same purpose.
data.common-project-operations#Common project: Method Endpoint Used for POST /api/v2/project/{project-slug}/envvar Create or replace a project environment variable. Body: {"name": "", "value": ""}. PATCH /api/v2/project/{provider}/{org}/{project}/settings Apply a partial update to project advanced settings. Body: {"advanced": { }}. POST /api/v2/webhook Create a webhook on a project. Body includes name, url, events, verify-tls, and scope (project UUID). The HMAC signing secret cannot be migrated — it must be set manually. POST /api/v2/project/{project-slug}/schedule Create a pipeline schedule on an OAuth project. Body includes name, description, timetable, parameters, and attribution-actor. PATCH /api/v2/org/{orgID}/project/{projectID}/oidc-custom-claims Write per-project OIDC audience and TTL.
data.deploys-read-only-export--sync#Deploys (:
The public Deploys v3 API is experimental and has no create endpoints.
Method Endpoint Used for GET https://app.circleci.com/api/v3/deploy/environments?filter[org_id]={orgUUID} List environments (paginated). GET https://app.circleci.com/api/v3/deploy/environments/{id} kind / description for one environment. GET https://app.circleci.com/api/v3/deploy/components?filter[org_id]={orgUUID} List components with their references.project.id. GET https://app.circleci.com/api/v3/deploy/settings?filter[project_id]={projectUUID} Per-project deploy/rollback pipelines.
data.download-the-artifact#Download the artif:
Method Endpoint Used for GET /api/v2/workflow/{workflow-id}/job List the jobs in a workflow. Used to identify the merge job by name. GET /api/v2/project/{project-slug}/{job-number}/artifacts List artifacts for a job. Used to locate the secrets.json artifact produced by the merge job. The artifact download itself (url from the artifacts list) is a direct GET with the Circle-Token header; no separate API client is required.
Error handling: if the pipeline run does not reach success within --poll-timeout (default 10 minutes), secrets capture exits with a non-zero status and prints the workflow and job state. The partially run pipeline is left in place for inspection; it is not cancelled automatically.
data.error-handling#Error handling: The HTTP client (api/rest) returns an HTTPError for any 4xx or 5xx response. The tool extracts the message field from JSON error bodies when present. Per-resource errors during export are recorded as warnings in the manifest rather than aborting the entire export. During sync, per-context and per-project errors are recorded in the report under error status and the remaining resources continue to be processed.
data.github-api#GitHub API: Method Endpoint Used for GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo} Resolve a GitHub repository's numeric ID (id field). Used when --github-token is set and a pipeline definition needs an external_id that was not captured, or a fresh one because the GitHub org changed. The request carries an Authorization: Bearer {token} header when a token is supplied. A 404 response means the repo is not in the destination GitHub org: the project is reported manual and its pipeline definition is skipped (no fallback to a stale captured id).
data.github-app-project-creation-and-enable-b: Method Endpoint Used for POST /api/v2/organization/{orgID}/project Create a GitHub App project by org UUID and name. Body: {"name": ""}. The orgID is the bare UUID (not a slug) for App-type orgs. Returns the new project's UUID. POST /api/v2/projects/{projUUID}/pipeline-definitions Create a pipeline definition on an App project. Body includes name, description, config_source (provider, repo external_id, file_path), and checkout_source. POST /api/v2/projects/{projUUID}/pipeline-definitions/{defUUID}/triggers Create a trigger on a pipeline definition. Created with disabled: true so no builds fire until explicitly enabled. Body includes event_source (provider plus repo.external_id, webhook.sender or schedule.{cron_expression,attribution_actor}), event_preset, checkout_ref, config_ref, event_name (webhook/schedule) and parameters (schedule). The API accepts no trigger name or description on create. PATCH /api/v2/projects/{projUUID}/triggers/{triggerUUID} Enable a trigger by setting disabled: false. This is the "enable builds" action for App projects — after this call, the trigger may fire on matching events. DELETE /api/v2/project/{slug} Delete a project. Used for rollback and test cleanup only. GitHub repository external_id: App pipeline definitions and triggers require a numeric GitHub repository ID (external_id). When the GitHub org is unchanged and the ID was captured in the manifest, it is reused directly (no GitHub call, no token). The tool calls the GitHub API (needs --github-token) only when the GitHub org changed, or when no ID was captured — an OAuth project whose App pipeline definition is synthesized.
data.groups#Groups: Method Endpoint Used for GET https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/groups List the org's CIAM groups (id, name). The "All members" group's UUID equals the org ID. POST https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/groups Create a group. Body: {"orgId": "...", "name": "...", "description": "..."}. POST https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/groups/{groupID}/add-users Add users to a group by UUID. Body: {"user_ids": [...]}.
data.oauth-project-creation-and-enable-builds: Method Endpoint Used for POST /api/v2/organization/{provider}/{org}/project Create a project shell in an OAuth org. Body: {"name": ""}. The project is created without a webhook; no builds fire until the project is followed. POST /api/v1.1/project/{vcsType}/{org}/{repo}/follow Follow a project. Installs a deploy key and webhook on the VCS repository. This is the "enable builds" action for OAuth projects — it may trigger an initial build.
data.org-level-role-grants#Org-level role gra: Method Endpoint Used for GET https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/role-grants List org-level role grants. Each item has user_id, email, username, and role (org-admin / org-contributor / org-viewer). Used both to capture source grants and to resolve destination user IDs by email. PUT https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/role-grants/user/{userID} Assign an org role to a user. Body: {"role": ""}. Automated by sync for users who already exist in the destination org (matched by email); unmatched users are reported as manual.
data.pagination#Pagination:
All paginated v2 endpoints follow the same pattern: the response includes a next_page_token field. When non-empty, the next request includes ?page-token=. circleci-migrate fetches all pages automatically.
The private /api/private/project endpoint uses the same next_page_token pattern but requires a page-size query parameter. The page size is capped at 50 to avoid server errors.
data.pipelines-api-secrets-capture#Pipelines: The secrets capture command drives a CircleCI pipeline run from the CLI without requiring a committed .circleci/config.yml. It uses the v2 Pipelines API to submit an inline (unversioned) config and then polls for completion:
data.poll-for-pipeline-status#Poll for pipeli: Method Endpoint Used for GET /api/v2/pipeline/{pipeline-id} Fetch pipeline metadata including state (created, errored, setup-pending, setup, pending, running, failing, failed, success, canceled). GET /api/v2/pipeline/{pipeline-id}/workflow List the workflows in a pipeline. Used to surface workflow-level errors to the user when a run fails.
data.private-ciam-endpoints-groups-and-sso#Pr:
These endpoints are served by app.circleci.com (not circleci.com). The api/org client maintains a separate HTTP client (app) that targets this host. The Circle-Token header is used identically.
Method Endpoint Used for GET https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/groups List the org's CIAM groups (named sets of members used for context group restrictions). GET https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/sso/enforced Read whether SSO login is enforced for the org. GET https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/sso/connection Read the org's SAML SSO connection body (realm, IdP fields). Returns HTTP 404 when no SSO is configured — treated as "not an error". Why SSO is capture-only: Recreating SSO on a destination org requires DNS TXT domain verification and IdP-side SAML app / iframe-origin setup. This cannot be automated via API. sync surfaces SSO state as a manual action in the report and never writes it. See your IdP and CircleCI SSO documentation for recreation steps.
data.private-ciam-role-grants-and-groups-appc:
These are private, unofficial endpoints. See the private-endpoint risk note below.
CIAM (Identity & Access Management) roles and groups are migrated for standalone circleci/-type orgs only. Like the CIAM group/SSO reads documented under Organization, these endpoints are served by app.circleci.com via the api/org client's separate app HTTP client. sync skips this section entirely on OAuth (gh/) orgs and when --skip-ciam is passed.
data.private-endpoint-risk-note#Private-endpo:
circleci-migrate is v2-first, but a handful of capabilities are only reachable through private, unofficial endpoints. These are not part of the documented public API and may change or disappear without notice. They are:
Surface Host / base Used for /api/private/project circleci.com Project discovery for GitHub App orgs (by org UUID). /private/ciam/... app.circleci.com CIAM groups, SSO state, and org/project role grants. /api/private/... org settings circleci.com Org contacts and other settings not yet promoted to v2. graphql-unstable circleci.com Orb-source introspection for orb inline. Implications for operators:
Treat any feature built on a private endpoint as best-effort. The tool records a warning and continues rather than aborting when one of these calls fails. A 4xx/5xx from a private endpoint is not necessarily a bug in the CLI — the endpoint contract may have shifted. Re-run with --debug to capture the request/response, and check for a newer release. This is the primary motivation for the planned migration off private endpoints (M4): public/GA replacements should be adopted as they become available.
data.project-discovery#Project discovery: Method Endpoint Used for GET /api/v1.1/projects List all projects the authenticated user follows. Used for OAuth org export; returns a flat JSON array (not paginated). GET /api/private/project?organization-id={orgID}&page-size=50 List all projects belonging to an org by UUID. Used for GitHub App org export. Covers both gh/ and circleci/ slugs. Paginated via next_page_token. Page size capped at 50 (server returns HTTP 500 for larger values). Why two endpoints? The v1.1 GET /projects endpoint covers OAuth orgs but returns only followed projects, and does not work for GitHub App orgs whose slugs use UUIDs. The private /api/private/project endpoint covers all org types by UUID and is used for App org export. For OAuth orgs where the source token's user does not follow every repository, pass an explicit --projects list to export.
data.project-level-role-grants-capture--manua: Method Endpoint Used for GET https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/projects/{projectID}/role-grants List per-project user role grants (user_id, email, username, role). GET https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/projects/{projectID}/groups List per-project group role grants (group_id, role). PUT https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/projects/{projectID}/role-grants/user/{userID} Assign a project role to a user. Body: {"role": ""}. (Client method exists; not driven automatically — see below.) POST https://app.circleci.com/private/ciam/orgs/{orgID}/projects/{projectID}/groups Grant a role to groups on a project. Body: {"group_ids": [...], "role": ""}. (Client method exists; not driven automatically — see below.) Why project-level grants are not applied automatically: the destination project UUID is not reliably mappable from the source, so sync records every per-project user and group grant as manual and the operator recreates them on the destination project (tracked in #179). The org-level role-grant and group write methods are driven automatically.
data.read-export-phase#Read (export phase): Method Endpoint Used for GET /api/v2/context?owner-id={id} List all contexts for an org. Paginated (page-token). GET /api/v2/context/{id}/environment-variable List env-var names for a context. Values are always masked. Paginated. GET /api/v2/context/{id}/restrictions List project, expression, and group restrictions. Returns restriction_type, restriction_value, and name. Paginated.
data.read-export-phase-1#Read (export phase): Method Endpoint Used for GET /api/v2/project/{project-slug} Fetch project metadata (name, ID, VCS info). Slug components are individually percent-encoded. GET /api/v2/project/{provider}/{org}/{project}/settings Read advanced project settings (autocancel_builds, build_fork_prs, etc.). Response is wrapped in an "advanced" key. GET /api/v2/project/{project-slug}/envvar List env-var names. The API returns a masked value ("xxxx1234") for each variable; stored as masked_value in the manifest. Paginated. GET /api/v2/project/{project-slug}/checkout-key List checkout/deploy key metadata (type, fingerprint, public key). Private key material is never returned. Paginated. GET /api/v2/webhook?scope-id={project-id}&scope-type=project List outbound webhooks scoped to a project. Requires the project UUID, not the slug. Paginated. GET /api/v2/project/{project-slug}/schedule List pipeline schedules. Paginated. GET /api/v2/projects/{projectID}/pipeline-definitions List App-pipeline definitions for a project. Each definition includes its config source, checkout source, and file path. Paginated. GET /api/v2/projects/{projectID}/pipeline-definitions/{defID}/triggers List the triggers attached to a pipeline definition. Returns event_source, event_preset, and disabled fields. Paginated. Also read from the destination on a sync re-run (together with the pipeline-definitions list) to reconcile what already exists. GET /api/v2/org/{orgID}/project/{projectID}/oidc-custom-claims Read per-project OIDC audience and TTL.
data.read-export-phase-2#Read (export phase): Method Endpoint Used for GET https://runner.circleci.com/api/v3/runner/resource?namespace={ns} List all resource classes registered under a namespace. Returns { "items": [...] }. namespace is a bare name (e.g. acme), not a slug. | GET | https://runner.circleci.com/api/v3/runner/resource-classes?filter[org_id]={orgUUID} | Sync only (read): classes attributed to an org (references.org.id). Used for the same-name-namespace handoff — attribution does not follow a namespace-owner change. | | GET | https://app.circleci.com/api/private/orb?org-id={orgUUID} | Sync only (read): orbs whose namespace the org owns; each carries namespace_name, which is how the syncer detects who owns a same-name namespace. |
data.runner-api-v3-self-hosted-runner-resourc:
Self-hosted runner resource classes have been migrated since v0.3.0. The runner API lives on its own host — https://runner.circleci.com — not on circleci.com. The api/runner client always targets runner.circleci.com regardless of --host (on Server installs the host is reused as-is). The same Circle-Token header is used.
Resource classes are keyed by namespace, and there is no clean org → namespace lookup in the API, so the namespace must be supplied explicitly: --runner-namespace on export, --dest-runner-namespace on sync. Only the class definition (resource_class, description) is captured; ephemeral runner instances are intentionally ignored, and no tokens are exported (runner registration tokens are never returned).
data.trigger-a-pipeline-with-inline-config#Tr:
Method Endpoint Used for POST /api/v2/project/{project-slug}/pipeline Trigger a new pipeline run. When the body includes a config field, the supplied YAML is used as the pipeline config rather than the repo's committed config. Request body:
{ "branch": "main", "config": "" } The inline config is generated at runtime: it contains one extraction job per context listed in the manifest (one context per job to guarantee variable isolation) and a final merge job that uploads secrets.json as an artifact.
data.usage-api-async-usage-export-job#Usage A:
The opt-in export --include-usage flow requests a historical usage report from the v2 Usage API. This is an asynchronous job: create the job, poll for completion, then download the resulting gzip-compressed CSV files. The window defaults to the last 30 days and may not exceed 31 days (server-enforced).
Method Endpoint Used for POST /api/v2/organizations/{orgID}/usage_export_job Submit a usage-export job. Body: {"start": "", "end": "", "shared_org_ids": [...]} (shared_org_ids optional). Returns usage_export_job_id. GET /api/v2/organizations/{orgID}/usage_export_job/{jobID} Poll job state; when completed, returns pre-signed download_urls. The CLI downloads each URL into a usage/ sub-directory next to the manifest. Local baseline only. Usage data is a record/baseline for the source org. It is never transferred to the destination by sync or migrate. If the export job fails or exceeds --usage-timeout (default 10 minutes), the main export still succeeds and a warning is printed.
data.v11-additional-ssh-keys#v1.1 additional:
Project additional SSH keys (keys added beyond the checkout/deploy key) are captured as metadata on export and re-uploaded on sync (skipped with --skip-extras). Private key material is never returned by any API, so it must be supplied to re-upload (the syncer matches by fingerprint to avoid duplicates).
Method Endpoint Used for GET /api/v1.1/project/{slug}/settings?ssh-key-digest=sha256 Read the ssh_keys array: hostname, public_key, and SHA256 fingerprint. Private keys are never present. POST /api/v1.1/project/{slug}/ssh-key Upload an additional SSH key. Body: {"hostname": "", "private_key": ""}. hostname may be empty for a globally-scoped key. Idempotent at the API level (re-uploading the same key is a no-op).
data.v11-org-settings-feature-flags#v1.1 org: Method Endpoint Used for GET /api/v1.1/organization/{vcsType}/{orgName}/settings Read the full org-level feature_flags map, including require_context_group_restriction and others. PUT /api/v1.1/organization/{vcsType}/{orgName}/settings Write feature flags to the destination org. Keys are converted from snake_case to kebab-case for the write path. Why v1.1? The feature_flags object is not exposed by the v2 API. This call is best-effort: if it fails (for example because the org is a GitHub App org with no v1.1 slug), a warning is recorded in the manifest and export continues.

flowchart TD START(["User commits manifest.json to source-org repo"]) START --> TRIGGER["Push triggers CircleCI pipeline in source org"] TRIGGER --> PARALLEL subgraph PARALLEL ["Parallel extract jobs — one per context"] J1["Job: extract-deploy-prodcontext: deploy-prod1. checkout2. orb: install circleci-migrate3. secrets extract --context deploy-prod4. persist bundle to workspace"] J2["Job: extract-sharedcontext: shared1. checkout2. orb: install circleci-migrate3. secrets extract --context shared4. persist bundle to workspace"] JN["... one job per context ..."] end PARALLEL --> MERGE MERGE["Job: merge(requires all extract jobs)1. attach_workspace2. circleci-migrate secrets merge -o secrets.json3. store_artifacts: secrets.json"] MERGE --> DOWNLOAD["User downloads secrets.json artifact from CircleCI UI"] DOWNLOAD --> NOTE["secrets.json contains plaintext valuesProtect it and do not commit it"]Why one job per context?
Each job can reference only the contexts listed under its context: key in the workflow. If two contexts define a variable with the same name, combining them in one job would cause one value to overwrite the other. Running one job per context guarantees isolation.
The secrets extract command reads variable names from manifest.json, looks each up in os.LookupEnv, and records found values in a SecretBundle JSON file. Variables not present in the environment are listed under "Not found" in the output (and cause a non-zero exit if --strict is passed).
After all extract jobs complete, the merge job combines the per-context bundles into a single secrets.json using secrets merge.

The orb inline command rewrites a CircleCI config file, replacing each private orb reference in the orbs: stanza with the orb's inlined YAML source. This is used during the namespace-transfer overlap window (e.g. while awesomecicd/ content is being moved to cci-labs/) to produce a config that works regardless of which namespace is active.

Key properties of the sync phase:
Dry run by default. No writes to CircleCI unless --apply is passed. Reviewing the dry-run output before applying is strongly recommended. Idempotent. Existing contexts and projects are reused by name. Re-running sync with --apply is safe — it will not duplicate resources or overwrite restrictions that already exist. Transparent report. Every action (created, exists, set, manual, error) is recorded and printed. Items requiring manual follow-up are surfaced explicitly.
data.secrets-capture--cli-orchestrated-flow-r:
secrets capture is the recommended capture path. It achieves the same result as the orb-based flow without requiring a committed .circleci/config.yml: the entire pipeline is generated at runtime and submitted as an inline (unversioned) config via the v2 Pipelines API.
flowchart TD START(["circleci-migrate secrets capture --org gh/acme --manifest manifest.json"]) START --> LOAD["Load manifest.jsonBuild list of contexts and projects to extract"] LOAD --> GEN["Generate inline pipeline config(one extract job per context, one merge job)"] GEN --> TRIGGER["POST /api/v2/project/slug/pipelinebody: branch + inline config YAMLReturns pipeline ID"] TRIGGER --> POLL subgraph POLL ["Poll until terminal state or --poll-timeout"] direction TB STATUS["GET /api/v2/pipeline/idCheck state field"] STATUS -->|"running / pending"| WAIT["Wait 5 s, retry"] WAIT --> STATUS STATUS -->|success| FETCH["Fetch artifact"] STATUS -->|"failed / errored"| FAIL["Exit non-zeroPrint workflow/job state"] end FETCH --> JOBS["GET /api/v2/pipeline/id/workflowGET /api/v2/workflow/wf-id/jobLocate merge job by name"] JOBS --> ARTIFACTS["GET /api/v2/project/slug/job-number/artifactsLocate secrets.json artifact URL"] ARTIFACTS --> DOWNLOAD["GET artifact URL (Circle-Token header)Write to --output path (mode 0600)"] DOWNLOAD --> DONE([Done — secrets.json ready for sync])Why this is the recommended path (vs. the orb-based alternative):
No .circleci/config.yml is committed to the repository. The inline config is ephemeral — it exists only for the duration of the run. --enable-trigger and --remove-restrictions allow the command to temporarily unlock contexts or triggers that would otherwise block the pipeline from running, restoring them after the run completes. --skip-restricted-contexts is a safer alternative: skip any context with active restrictions rather than modifying them.

data: The docs site is Hugo and the Hextra theme, built from the Markdown in this repository. CircleCI builds it on every branch and publishes it to GitHub Pages from main.
data.add-or-move-a-page#Add or move a page:
List the page in site/nav.txt, in the group where it belongs. site/stage.sh fails on a docs/**/*.md file that nav.txt misses and on a listed file that does not exist. docs/cli/*.md is generated: never edit it by hand.
Site-only pages, such as the plan builder, live in site/pages/ and are staged at the top of the site (site/pages/plan.md is /plan/).
data.how-ci-builds-and-publishes-it#How CI bu:
The workflow docs-site in .circleci/continue_config.yml has two jobs:
docs-site-build runs on every branch with no context. It tests the plan builder (node --test site/tests/), stages the Markdown, runs hugo --minify --panicOnWarning and checks the links with site/check.sh. Hugo, lychee and Node are pinned and SHA-256 verified. docs-site-publish runs on main only, after the build. It pushes the built site to the gh-pages branch with site/publish.sh. Without GITHUB_TOKEN it publishes nothing and says so.
data.moving-to-circleci-labs#Moving to Circle:
The site works the same under the CircleCI-Labs organization. Change these four things:
In site/hugo.yaml, set baseURL to https://circleci-labs.github.io// and the GitHub menu url to the new repository. The footer, stage.sh and publish.sh read that URL. Change the site link in README.md. Create the docs-site-publish context for the new project, merge to main, and enable Pages again with the gh api command above (new owner in the path). Add an entry for the project to data/projects.yaml in CircleCI-Labs/circleci-labs.github.io, then build and push that hub. GitHub redirects the repository URL after a transfer, but not the old Pages path. Update the links that point to the old site.
data.one-time-setup#One-time setup:
Create a CircleCI context named docs-site-publish with GITHUB_TOKEN, a fine-grained token with Contents: write on this repository. Merge to main. The first publish creates the gh-pages branch. Turn on GitHub Pages with gh-pages and / as the source: echo '{"source":{"branch":"gh-pages","path":"/"}}' \ | gh api -X POST "repos/AwesomeCICD/circleci-org-migration-cli/pages" --input - If Pages already exists, use -X PUT. Send the JSON body as shown: with -f "source[path]=/" the API ignores the path.
Check: https://awesomecicd.github.io/circleci-org-migration-cli/ loads, in light and dark mode.
data.preview-it#Preview it:
Install Hugo extended 0.168.0 and Go, then run:
make site-serve # stage the Markdown and serve http://localhost:1313/ make site-check # build, then check every link and heading anchor offline (needs lychee 0.24.2) Restage after you edit a page: stop the server and run make site-serve again. site/stage.sh copies the pages into site/content/ (not tracked). It never changes the sources.
Check: make site ends with no warning. A warning fails the build.
data.upgrade-a-pinned-tool#Upgrade a pinned t: The versions of Hugo, lychee and Node are in the docs-site command and the docs-site-build job. A new version needs its new SHA-256 value too, from the release checksums. The Hextra version is in site/go.mod and site/go.sum.

Testing instructions — including how the e2e fixtures are structured and how to run a manual dry-run or --apply migration against a dummy org — now live in the End-to-end and manual testing section of CONTRIBUTING.md. The test topology is described in e2e-fixtures.yaml at the repo root.
Install Choose a migration What moves Plan builder: Generate the exact commands and manual steps for your CircleCI org migration, in order.

Find your source org's slug (Organization Settings > Overview), then follow the arrows to a runbook. A slug starting with gh/ or bb/ is an OAuth org. A slug starting with circleci/ is a GitHub App or standalone org.
flowchart TD S{"Source org slug"} -->|"gh/ or bb/"| D1{"Destination slug"} S -->|"circleci/"| D2{"Destination slug"} D1 -->|"gh/ or bb/"| R1["OAuth to OAuth"] D1 -->|"circleci/"| R2["OAuth to GitHub App"] D2 -->|"circleci/"| R3["App to App"] D2 -->|"gh/ or bb/"| R4["No runbook: ask support"] M{"One GitHub org has both?"} -->|"yes"| T["Two legs: one runbook each"]If one GitHub org has both an OAuth record and an App record, CircleCI keeps them as two orgs. Migrate each as its own leg.
Scenario Runbook Rename or consolidate GitHub OAuth orgs (gh/ to gh/) OAuth to OAuth Repos moved to a new GitHub org, OAuth on both sides OAuth to OAuth Bitbucket OAuth to Bitbucket OAuth (bb/ to bb/) OAuth to OAuth Legacy OAuth org to a GitHub App org (gh/ to circleci/) OAuth to GitHub App GitHub App or standalone org to another (circleci/ to circleci/) App to App App org, repos moved to a new GitHub org App to App Mixed org: OAuth record plus App record One runbook per leg How long it takes depends on your org. Plan a freeze window long enough for the steps marked Cutover. A dry run against a test org tells you how long they take, because the secrets transfer runs one pipeline per project.
Not sure what is in your org? Run circleci-migrate export --source-org <slug> and read migration-report.md. It is read-only.
To get the commands filled in for your own org slugs, use the plan builder on the docs site. It runs in your browser and never asks for a token.
Next: install the CLI, then see what moves.
Install with Homebrew on macOS or Linux, or download a signed binary for any platform. Then check the version.
data.as-a-plugin-to-the-circleci-cli#As a plu:
If you use the official circleci CLI, run circleci run migrate . It starts circleci-migrate from your PATH and passes your configured token and host. Bare circleci migrate is not supported.
Next: choose your migration.
data.behind-a-proxy-or-allowlist#Behind a pro:
Allow these hosts for the install method you use.
Method Hosts Release download api.github.com, github.com, release-assets.githubusercontent.com Homebrew The hosts above, plus formulae.brew.sh and raw.githubusercontent.com go install github.com, proxy.golang.org, sum.golang.org, filippo.io, golang.org, gopkg.in, go.yaml.in If only github.com is reachable, GOPROXY=off go install github.com/AwesomeCICD/circleci-org-migration-cli@ fetches straight from the repository. Go still needs the vanity-import hosts, because it reads their go-import metadata over HTTPS even with the proxy off. Behind a corporate proxy, set HTTPS_PROXY or GOPROXY=https:// first.
Building from source (git clone, then go build -o circleci-migrate .) needs github.com for the clone and the same hosts for dependencies. The repository does not ship a vendor/ directory, so GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor works only if you vendor the tree yourself with go mod vendor.
data.macos-and-linux#macOS and Linux:
brew install AwesomeCICD/tap/circleci-migrate circleci-migrate version No Homebrew? Download the release archive for your platform:
VERSION=$(curl -sfL https://api.github.com/repos/AwesomeCICD/circleci-org-migration-cli/releases/latest \ | grep '"tag_name"' | head -1 | cut -d'"' -f4) OS=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]') ARCH=$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/; s/aarch64/arm64/') curl -sfL "https://github.com/AwesomeCICD/circleci-org-migration-cli/releases/download/${VERSION}/circleci-migrate_${VERSION#v}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz" | tar -xz sudo install -m 0755 circleci-migrate /usr/local/bin/ circleci-migrate version Check: version prints the release you installed.
data.tokens-and-hosts#Tokens and hosts:
Each command reads these environment variables. A flag overrides the variable.
Variable Used for CIRCLECI_SOURCE_TOKEN Reading the source org (--source-token) CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN Writing the destination org (--dest-token) CIRCLECI_CLI_TOKEN or CIRCLE_TOKEN Fallback for both sides (--token) GITHUB_TOKEN Looking up GitHub repo IDs when needed (--github-token) CIRCLECI_CLI_HOST, CIRCLECI_HOST or CIRCLE_URL Host URL for CircleCI Server (--host) Create tokens under User Settings > Personal API Tokens. The token's user must be an admin of the org it acts on. The host defaults to https://circleci.com.
data.verify-the-download#Verify the download:
Every release archive has a .bundle file next to it. It holds a Sigstore signature made keylessly by CircleCI's release pipeline. Download both, then verify with cosign v3:
cosign verify-blob circleci-migrate___.tar.gz \ --bundle circleci-migrate___.tar.gz.bundle \ --certificate-oidc-issuer https://oidc.circleci.com \ --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://circleci\.com/api/v2/projects/.*' Check: cosign prints Verified OK. Do not run a binary that fails this check.
The certificate records the exact CircleCI pipeline definition that built the release, and the signature is logged on the public Rekor transparency log. To pin to that project, read the identity from the bundle, then replace --certificate-identity-regexp with --certificate-identity :
jq -r '.verificationMaterial.certificate.rawBytes' circleci-migrate___.tar.gz.bundle \ | base64 -d | openssl x509 -inform DER -noout -text | grep URI The URL has the form https://circleci.com/api/v2/projects//pipeline-definitions/.
data.windows-powershell#Windows (PowerShell): $Version = (Invoke-RestMethod https://api.github.com/repos/AwesomeCICD/circleci-org-migration-cli/releases/latest).tag_name $Arch = if ($env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE -eq 'ARM64') { 'arm64' } else { 'amd64' } $Zip = "circleci-migrate_$($Version.TrimStart('v'))_windows_$Arch.zip" Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/AwesomeCICD/circleci-org-migration-cli/releases/download/$Version/$Zip" -OutFile $Zip Expand-Archive $Zip -DestinationPath "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\circleci-migrate" -Force & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\circleci-migrate\circleci-migrate.exe" version Add %LOCALAPPDATA%\circleci-migrate to your PATH to run circleci-migrate from anywhere. In PowerShell, set tokens with $env:CIRCLECI_SOURCE_TOKEN = "" instead of export.
data.with-go#With Go: go install github.com/AwesomeCICD/circleci-org-migration-cli@latest This needs Go 1.26 or later.

Names, structure and settings move on their own. Secret values move with one extra command. A short list has to be done by hand.
Read each row as: does it move automatically, does it need a step in your runbook, or do you do it yourself. Nothing is ever deleted from the source org.
Item Moves automatically Moves with a step Do by hand Contexts and variable names sync Context secret values secrets transfer Treat every value as exposed once moved: rotate it Context restrictions: project and expression sync remaps projects by name Context restrictions: group Automatic only if a group of the same name exists in the destination Otherwise recreate in the destination UI Project settings sync OAuth-only settings with no App equivalent are dropped: fork-PR builds, fork-PR secrets, pr_only_branch_overrides OSS flag App projects detect it from repo visibility. For an OAuth destination with a public repo, set "Free and Open Source" in Advanced settings Project env vars Names via sync Values via secrets transfer --include-project-vars Additional SSH keys secrets transfer --include-ssh-keys Checkout and deploy keys Created when an OAuth project is followed Private keys are never exportable. App destinations need none. Re-add manually uploaded deploy keys on OAuth Pipeline definitions and triggers (App destinations) sync creates them, disabled cutover --enable-dest turns them on A plain OAuth project gets one synthesized build-and-test definition. Add others by hand. Trigger names are assigned by CircleCI Schedules sync Webhooks sync recreates them --webhook-secrets-out writes the new outbound signing secrets and inbound URLs Give every sender and receiver the new value. Without the flag, secrets are empty Environments and hierarchies sync, by name If the API rejects the write, create them under Deploys. Components appear on the first circleci run release plan. Deploy history stays in the source Orbs and namespace A different destination namespace is republished by sync A same-name namespace is moved by CircleCI support. Rewrite orb references if you changed namespace Runner resource classes sync --dest-runner-namespace After a same-name namespace move the classes stay attributed to the source: delete the copies, re-run sync, issue new tokens Runner instances and tokens Never move. Register agents against the destination classes Org roles and groups App and standalone orgs, for users already in the destination (--skip-ciam leaves them alone) Add users to the destination first, then re-run sync Per-project role grants Recreate on each destination project SSO (SAML) DNS verification and IdP setup. New SSO users default to Viewer: set Contributor for people who trigger pipelines Org settings sync: feature flags, OIDC claims, URL-orb allow list, config policies, contacts, retention, budgets, release tracker, block-unregistered-users --include-danger-flags after you validate OpenTelemetry exporter headers, audit-log streaming Exporter config via sync Re-add header values. Recreate streams against destination-owned infrastructure Cloud OIDC trust policies, IP allowlists Update them for the new org ID and ranges Plan and billing Ask CircleCI support to move the plan. The destination should be on the Free plan and not share another org's plan Project API tokens sync --create-project-tokens mints new values Repoint every consumer of the old token Personal API tokens Each user creates their own for the new org Insights, build history, usage data Do not move. export --include-usage saves a local usage snapshot only IDs and slugs New project, context and pipeline IDs are assigned, and gh/acme/web becomes circleci/<org>/<project> for App destinations. Update anything that hard-codes the old ones Secret values are never readable through the API. secrets transfer copies them from inside a pipeline, straight to the destination, and never writes them to disk. See secrets.
Moving from OAuth to a GitHub App loses a few settings that have no equivalent. The OAuth to GitHub App runbook lists them.
OAuth to GitHub App OAuth to OAuth App to App

Use this runbook to move one GitHub App or standalone org (circleci/…) to another (circleci/…): a consolidation, a split, or a move to a new GitHub org. Do the prep ahead of time, then run the cutover inside a freeze window.
data.1-run-preflight#1. Run preflight:
Catch bad tokens and unreachable orgs early. doctor is read-only.
circleci-migrate doctor --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG" Check: it exits 0 with no hard failures.
data.10-add-pipeline-definitions-and-triggers:
Triggers are created disabled. New webhook URLs and secrets go to webhook-secrets.json (mode 0600). Answer N at the "Enable N trigger(s)" prompt, because cutover enables them in step 12.
circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \ --skip-orb --skip-runner --apply --webhook-secrets-out webhook-secrets.json Check: no line says "connect the repo to the GitHub App". If one does, connect the repo and re-run.
data.11-move-orbs-and-runners-only-if-you-use:
A namespace belongs to one org. Ask CircleCI support to move a same-name namespace, and orb references need no change. For a different namespace, republish. Resource classes are recreated, but runner instances never move, so register agents with new tokens.
circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \ --only orb --dest-orb-namespace --apply circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \ --only runner --dest-runner-namespace --apply Check: runners show online, and validate lists the orbs (see Verify). Update cloud OIDC trust policies for the new org ID.
data.12-enable-the-destination#12. Enable the:
This enables only the triggers that were enabled in the source. Do not run sync --apply --yes here: it enables triggers without pausing the source, so both orgs build.
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --enable-dest circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --enable-dest --apply Check: no project reports manual. If one does, enable that trigger in Project Settings > Triggers. See cutover.
data.2-export-the-source#2. Export the source:
Export records names and structure, never secret values, and is read-only. Run it while the source still has its pipelines, so the definitions are captured.
circleci-migrate export --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --output manifest.json --report migration-report.md Add --runner-namespace for self-hosted runners and --orb-namespace for orbs.
Check: read migration-report.md in full and note the counts of contexts, projects and project env vars.
data.3-write-mappingjson#3. Write mapping.jso:
Without org.to, sync writes to your source org. The org line is all you need, because projects are matched by name.
cat > mapping.json <
data.4-create-the-migration-secrets-context#4:
Secret values can only be read inside a pipeline. The transfer pipeline runs in the source org and gets the destination token from a context. In the source org, go to Organization Settings > Contexts and create migration-secrets with one variable, CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN, set to the destination token.
Check: the context exists in the source org with that one variable.
data.5-dry-run-the-cutover-commands#5. Dry-ru:
Every command below is a dry run until you add --apply. Read each plan now.
circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --skip-pipelines --skip-orb --skip-runner circleci-migrate secrets transfer --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \ --dest-org-id "$DEST_ORG_ID" --dest-token-context migration-secrets \ --include-project-vars --include-ssh-keys --remove-restrictions circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source Check: no unexplained error lines. Every project shows SKIP in the transfer plan because the destination projects do not exist yet. That is expected.
data.6-freeze-merges-and-create-the-destinati:
Stop merges in the source repos so nothing lands between the transfer and the switch. Then create the projects: project env vars are written into them, so they must exist first. This creates projects, contexts, settings, org roles and groups, but no pipelines or triggers.
circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \ --skip-pipelines --skip-orb --skip-runner --apply Check: every project reports skipped: --skip-pipelines, and the team confirms the freeze. Re-run the step 5 transfer dry run: no project shows SKIP now.
data.7-transfer-the-secrets#7. Transfer the s:
This runs one pipeline per source project and writes each value straight to the destination over TLS. Nothing touches disk. It must run before you pause the source, because a paused project drops the pipeline. If your repos move to a new GitHub org, run it before they move, because the pipelines check out code from the old org.
circleci-migrate secrets transfer --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \ --dest-org-id "$DEST_ORG_ID" --dest-token-context migration-secrets \ --include-project-vars --include-ssh-keys --remove-restrictions \ --enable-trigger --apply Check: the log reports every context and project pipeline succeeded. See secrets.
data.8-pause-the-source#8. Pause the source:
Pausing stops builds in the source and records every change in cutover-state.json, so you can undo it. Preview first.
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source --apply Check: every source project is listed as paused, and cutover-state.json exists. Keep it until the cutover is confirmed.
data.9-connect-the-repos-to-the-destination#9:
Definitions can only be created for repos the destination GitHub App can see.
New GitHub org: confirm every repo is connected in the destination org's GitHub App installation. Nothing is uninstalled. Same GitHub org: uninstall the CircleCI GitHub App from the source org's connection, then install it from the destination org with every migrating repo selected. Users click Authorize, then Refresh permissions if Projects is empty. Caution Same GitHub org only. Uninstalling deletes the source org's GitHub App pipelines and triggers, and the export is the only record of them. cutover --undo can no longer re-enable them.
Check: the destination org lists every repo as connected.
Tip New GitHub org only: if you created definitions and triggers earlier (a sync --apply without --skip-pipelines), the pause and the enable can run as one command: cutover --pause-source --enable-dest --apply. Run the transfer first.
data.at-a-glance#At a glance: flowchart LR subgraph prep ["Prep (days before)"] direction TB A["Doctor, export"] --> B["mapping.json,secrets context"] --> C["Dry run"] end subgraph before ["Cutover: source still live"] direction TB D["Freeze merges,create projects"] --> E["Transfer secrets"] --> F["Pause source"] end subgraph after ["Cutover: destination"] direction TB H["Add pipelinesand triggers"] --> I["Enable destination"] --> J["Smoke test, validate"] end prep --> before --> G["Connect repossame GitHub org: move App,POINT OF NO RETURN"] --> after classDef ponr fill:#b42318,stroke:#7a1a12,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff class G ponrIf your repos move to a new GitHub org, step 9 uninstalls nothing and there is no point of no return.
data.before-you-start#Before you start: You are an admin of both CircleCI orgs, the destination org exists, and you have a personal API token for each (User Settings > Personal API Tokens). The CLI is installed (install). circleci-migrate version prints v0.19.0 or later. Every user whose org role should move is already a member of the destination org. Roles apply only to existing members, matched by email. Pass --skip-ciam to sync to leave roles and groups alone. Repos moving to a new GitHub org: a GitHub token with repo read, and the CircleCI GitHub App installed in the new GitHub org from the destination CircleCI org. Same GitHub org: you can install and uninstall the CircleCI GitHub App in it. A GitHub org connects to one CircleCI org at a time.
data.if-something-fails#If something fails: Error Fix Pipeline definition is manual: connect the repo Connect the repo to the destination GitHub App and re-run sync --apply. source project(s) are paused Run the transfer before the pause, or run cutover --undo --apply and retry. Org roles missing in the destination The user is not yet a destination member. Add them, then re-run sync --apply. Wrong repo IDs after a GitHub org move Set GITHUB_TOKEN and pass --dest-github-org to sync. More in troubleshooting. Flags: sync, secrets transfer, cutover.
data.if-your-org-is-mixed-oauth-and-app#If yo:
When one GitHub org has both integrations, CircleCI keeps two org records: gh/ and circleci/. Migrate each as its own leg, with its own manifest, mapping and state file.
OAuth leg: follow OAuth to GitHub App, or OAuth to OAuth if the destination is OAuth. App leg: follow this runbook. Add --skip-org-settings to its sync commands if the first leg already wrote the org settings, and --state cutover-state-app.json to every cutover command.
data.roll-back#Roll back:
Before the App moves in step 9, undo everything. This restores the source flags and triggers and disables the destination triggers it enabled.
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --undo --apply After a same-GitHub-org App move, --undo restores only the drop-all-build-requests flag. It does not move the App. To return, uninstall it from the destination org and reinstall it from the source.
data.set-up#Set up: export SOURCE_ORG="circleci/" export DEST_ORG="circleci/" export DEST_ORG_ID="" export CIRCLECI_SOURCE_TOKEN="" export CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN="" export GITHUB_TOKEN="" # only if repos move to a new GitHub org $SOURCE_ORG = "circleci/" $DEST_ORG = "circleci/" $DEST_ORG_ID = "" $env:CIRCLECI_SOURCE_TOKEN = "" $env:CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN = "" $env:GITHUB_TOKEN = "" # only if repos move to a new GitHub org Find an org ID under Organization Settings > Overview. Commands use \ to continue lines. In PowerShell, end the line with a backtick instead.
data.verify#Verify:
Push a commit to a migrated repo. Check: a pipeline starts in the destination org, runs green, and a job can read a context variable.
circleci-migrate validate --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG" \ --mapping mapping.json --dest-token-context migration-secrets A clean report exits 0 and lists only expected manual items: SSO, role bindings and per-project grants. Add --dest-runner-namespace and --dest-orb-namespace to compare runners and orbs. Then clean up:
Give each webhook sender and receiver its new value from webhook-secrets.json, then delete the file. Recreate per-project role grants in the destination. Rotate every transferred secret. Rotate the destination token and delete the migration-secrets context. Update badges, Slack apps and required status checks for the new project slugs.
data.what-moves#What moves: Moves automatically: contexts, projects, project and org settings, pipeline definitions, triggers and schedules (created disabled), org roles and groups, runner resource classes. Needs a step: secret values and SSH keys, webhook secrets and URLs, orbs and runner instances (step 11). Does not move: per-project role grants, SSO, build history, and group context restrictions unless the group exists in the destination. The full list is in what moves.

data: Use this runbook to move a GitHub OAuth org (gh/…) to a standalone GitHub App org (circleci/…). Do the prep ahead of time, including the support requests, then run the cutover inside a freeze window.

Catch bad tokens and unreachable orgs before you touch anything. doctor is read-only.
circleci-migrate doctor --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG" Check: it exits 0 with no hard failures.
data.10-move-the-github-app#10. Move the GitH:
A GitHub org connects to one CircleCI org at a time. Uninstall the CircleCI GitHub App from the source org's connection. Then install it from the destination org on the same GitHub org, with every migrating repo selected. Each user opens the new org and clicks Authorize, then Refresh permissions if Projects is empty.
Caution Point of no return. Uninstalling deletes the source org's GitHub App pipelines and triggers, and the export is the only record of them. cutover --undo can no longer re-enable them.
Now ask CircleCI support to move the plan to the destination org, and carry on while they work.
Check: the destination org lists every repo as connected, and support confirms the plan request. A repo that is not connected still gets a project, but its definition is created only after you connect it and re-run sync in the next step.
data.11-add-pipeline-definitions-and-triggers:

Resource classes are recreated, but runner instances never move, so register agents with new tokens. After a namespace move the classes stay attributed to the source: delete the copies, re-run this sync, then issue new tokens.

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --enable-dest circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --enable-dest --apply Check: no project reports manual. If one does, enable that trigger in Project Settings > Triggers. See cutover.

Check: read migration-report.md in full and note the counts of contexts, projects and project env vars.

The mapping tells sync which org to write to. The org line is all you need, because App projects are matched by name.
cat > mapping.json <

Check: the context exists in the source org with that one variable.

The plan, and any same-name orb namespace, cannot move through the API. Tell support the destination org ID and the date you will move the GitHub App. The destination org must be on the Free plan and not share another org's plan.
Check: support confirms they will run it after the App moves.

Every command below is a dry run until you add --apply. Read each plan now.
circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --skip-pipelines --skip-orb --skip-runner circleci-migrate secrets transfer --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \ --dest-org-id "$DEST_ORG_ID" --dest-token-context migration-secrets \ --include-project-vars --include-ssh-keys --remove-restrictions circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source Check: no unexplained error lines. data.9-pause-the-source#9. Pause the source:
Pausing stops builds in the source and records every change in cutover-state.json, so you can undo it. Preview first.
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source --apply Check: every source project is listed as paused, and cutover-state.json exists. Keep it until the cutover is confirmed.
